Reguliersdwarsstraat (w01-194.alt.jpg, 43 px/m): the ground storey has three bands, not two: the two doors (the side door at the left end, the 7.1 m staff entrance at the right), the five bays of the stone grid (each a field of small windows in two rows, counted per bay as the counter did) and the five recessed entresol bays; the 3.3 m louvre over the staff entrance is a steel grille, not an opening; then three raster storeys of 14 (the glazed spandrel under each is a separate low band the counter folded into its storey). Singel (w02-1.jpg 2021 and .alt 2017): the Bloemenmarkt stalls hide the ground storey in both captures, so the measured face starts at 6 m (heightM); the raster continues past the crop's left edge across the w03-359 jog, and the crop cuts a window there (55 px = 1.1 m in 2021), so the measured span starts at the first whole pier (12.3 m along the north face, alongM) and counts the counter's 9 axes: 8 whole windows and the narrower end window against the Carlton (1.7-1.8 m). The set-back storey under the floating cornice is one glazed ribbon behind the posts (the counter's 1; the posts and mullions are under the 0.3 m ribbon rule). The Singel bearing was 12 degrees; the wall faces 1 degree (brief: w02-1 N 1), and at 12 the elevation sheared the set-back storey 3.7 m behind the posts sideways by 0.7 m. On the Reguliersdwarsstraat the set-back storey stands 3 m behind the parapet and the street crop does not show it (sky between the rooftop frames in 2019 and 2025), so the measured face stops at the raster's top band (heightM 17.6 m), as the counter's null says.
